topic: designers and creators struggling to keep a character, style, or brand consistent across many AI-generated outputs
blind_spots: No quantitative data on how frequently consistency failures occur or how much time/cost they impose on creators.
No direct evidence from end consumers about whether they actually perceive the character/brand drift that creators worry about.
Little evidence on whether newer reference-input or character-reference features actually solve the problem in practice.
No coverage of non-image modalities (e.g., video, 3D, audio) where consistency may also matter.
Several listed evidence items (AI mastery, AI simp farms, junior pipeline, designer job market) are unrelated to consistency and provide no usable signal on this pain point.
contradictions: Evidence frames consistency failures as fundamentally a model architecture issue (memoryless sampling) while other items frame failures as 'environment design' failures rather than model failures, implying different root causes and fixes.

Industry blogs imply brand consistency can be fixed with playbooks/workflows, while the technical-community evidence suggests the memoryless nature of generation is an inherent limitation requiring per-call re-anchoring.
